A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 19-page versions of the same LaRoSA paper. The main text, figures, tables, equations, algorithm, and Appendices A-C support a reliable full comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original perplexity, task-accuracy, inference-speed, and ablation results in Section 5, with additional empirical analyses and full results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and outcomes, including the main evaluations, ablations, and appendix results.

M1.justification: The PCA-derived layerwise rotations, residual adapters, Top-K sparsification, coefficient grid search, and customized GEMV kernel remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WikiText2 evaluation, seven zero-shot tasks, MMLU, MATH500, GPQA-Diamond, and AIME'24, alongside the same calibration and inference-speed datasets. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: CATS, TEAL, and dense-model comparisons retain the same participation in Tables 1-2 and Appendix C. The ablation comparators and RTN, GPTQ, AWQ, and OmniQuant comparisons in Table 9 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain identical, including 16 calibration sequences of 2048 tokens, 128 WikiText2 evaluation samples, zero-shot and five-shot protocols, model configurations, and full prefill-token sparsification. Speed-evaluation procedures are also retained.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same sparsification-function, rotation-granularity, calibration-data, and quantization analyses in Section 5.3, coefficient analysis in Appendix B, and theoretical-versus-empirical error comparison in Figure 5.

E5.justification: The sparsity variability reported with plus/minus values in Table 5 is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, both report LLaMA2-7B at 40% sparsity with LaRoSA perplexity 5.64 in Table 2 and average zero-shot accuracy 66.15 in Table 1.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations remain unchanged, including computational invariance in Section 3.2, Theorem A.1 and its proof, and the coefficient constraints in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims of training-free activation sparsification, consistent sparsity, limited performance degradation, and reliable inference acceleration. The source-code link does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of threshold mismatch, calibration robustness, and quantization compatibility are retained. The discussions of residual-adapter overhead and restrictions on rotating particular activations are also unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code link to the alibaba/EfficientAI repository in the abstract; v1 has no corresponding implementation link. Hardware, computation time, calibration details, and Appendix B hyperparameters remain unchanged. Repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with activation-sparsity methods and connections to SliceGPT, QuaRot, and SpinQuant. The new implementation link does not introduce related research.

P1.justification: v2 adds the source-code sentence, changes several cross-references from 'Appendix' to 'Section,' and removes the parenthetical expansion '(SOTA)' in Section 5.1. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract text produces limited column and page-flow shifts near the beginning. Table 1's caption changes its appendix-reference wording. All five figures and nineteen tables retain their displays, numbering, and substantive content.

improvement.justification: The source-code location added to the abstract modestly improves implementation discoverability and reproducibility guidance. Scientific evidence, methods, theory, and conclusions remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited to access information; the PDFs do not establish repository completeness or usability.
